title: Comprehensive framework for evaluation of deep neural networks in detection and quantification of lymphoma from PET/CT images: clinical insights, pitfalls, and observer agreement analyses
abstract: arXiv:2311.09614v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This study addresses critical gaps in automated lymphoma segmentation from PET/CT images, focusing on issues often overlooked in existing literature. While deep learning has been applied for lymphoma lesion segmentation, few studies incorporate out-of-distribution testing, raising concerns about model generalizability across diverse imaging conditions and patient populations. We highlight the need to compare model performance with expert human annotators, including intra- and inter-observer variability, to understand task difficulty better. Most approaches focus on overall segmentation accuracy but overlook lesion-specific measures important for precise lesion detection and disease quantification. To address these gaps, we propose a clinically relevant framework for evaluating deep segmentation networks. translated_title: 淋巴瘤PET/CT图像检测与定量中深度神经网络评估的综合框架：临床见解、陷阱与观察者一致性分析
translated_abstract: 本研究针对PET/CT图像中自动化淋巴瘤分割的关键空白，聚焦于现有文献中常被忽视的问题。尽管深度学习已应用于淋巴瘤病灶分割，但很少有研究纳入分布外测试，这引发了对模型在不同成像条件和患者群体中泛化能力的担忧。我们强调需要将模型性能与专家人工标注者进行比较，包括观察者内和观察者间的变异性，以更好地理解任务难度。大多数方法侧重于整体分割准确性，却忽视了对于精确病灶检测和疾病定量至关重要的病灶特异性指标。为解决这些空白，我们提出了一个临床相关的深度分割网络评估框架。利用这种病灶指标特异性评估，我们评估了四个深度网络（ResUNet, SegResNet, DynUNet）的性能。
tldr: 本文提出了一个临床相关的评估框架，强调通过病灶特异性指标、分布外测试和与专家标注者比较，全面评估淋巴瘤PET/CT分割网络的性能，填补了现有研究中的关键空白。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a clinically relevant evaluation framework that emphasizes lesion-specific metrics, out-of-distribution testing, and comparison with expert annotators to comprehensively assess lymphoma PET/CT segmentation networks, addressing key gaps in existing research.
